Title: ChatGPT vs. Gemini 3: la genial carrera para ser la mejor IA

Summary: 
The competition for leadership in artificial intelligence intensifies as Google's new Gemini 3 model surpasses OpenAI's ChatGPT in certain benchmarks, challenging OpenAI's dominance since the 2022 launch of ChatGPT. OpenAI, which initially led the AI race due to superior models, now faces pressure from Google’s extensive resources, including massive user bases, powerful computational infrastructure, and broad distribution networks. In contrast, Google has multiple revenue streams. Meanwhile, China is emerging as a strong competitor, with Baidu launching DeepSeek, a model claimed to match GPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Pro, and adopting a strategy of low pricing in Western markets—similar to past strategies in solar energy, steel, and electric vehicles. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang warned that China is just nanoseconds behind the U.S. in AI development. Analysts predict Google may maintain the best model in 2026. The market is expected to split between cost-effective, specialized small models and high-end, complex models like those from OpenAI, with no single model likely to replace the other. As Cox concludes, 'The more intelligence available, the more applications will emerge.'
